grounding.quote:
This profile owns only the application-neutral record, relation, identity,
causal, effect-boundary, frontier and refusal laws above.

concepts.label: Traversal-occurrence profile
concepts.definition: Application-neutral traversal-occurrence profile owning record, relation, identity, causal, effect-boundary, frontier and refusal laws. It supplies no operation or judgment authority and is available but inactive for a Product without complete Product adoption.

grounding.quote: The core constraint kinds are (P3, P5):

concepts.label: Occurrence constraint, judgment, residual and stop domains
concepts.definition: Closed constraint kinds: identity_dependency_acyclic, occurrence_causation_acyclic, event_causation_acyclic, occurrence_seed_complete, relation_claim_admissible, semantic_cut_complete, pre_effect_current, operation_grant_contains_effect, event_scope_compatible, frontier_complete, transition_subject_complete. Closed judgment kinds: model_validation, occurrence_admission, event_admission, claim_admission, semantic_cut_admission, effect_readiness, transition_evaluation, frontier_projection. Closed residual kinds: unobserved_subject_state, partial_effect, unresolved_cause, unresolved_scope, competing_lineage, stale_frontier, stale_currentness, unobserved_external_mutation. Closed stop kinds: hold, gap, refusal, invalid_basis, out_of_scope, partial_effect.

concepts.label: Mutable subject W
concepts.definition: Externally mutable subject W, observed under stable SubjectBinding b_W. W remains the carrier of mutable reality; observations, evidence, results, checkpoints, events, projections, caches and model content describe it without replacing it.

grounding.quote:
The stable concept identity does not identify one immutable profile
edition.
TraversalOccurrenceSignature = {

concepts.label: TraversalOccurrenceSignature and exact profile basis
concepts.definition: Stable concept identity differs from an immutable profile edition. TraversalOccurrenceSignature has exact kind stdo.traversal-occurrence-signature, schema_version 1, calculus_basis_identity, calculus_signature_schema_clause_ref, occurrence_signature_clause_refs and profile_member_sha256. Its identity is sha256(JCS(TraversalOccurrenceSignature)). TraversalOccurrenceProfileBasis has exact kind stdo.traversal-occurrence-profile-basis, schema_version 1, concept_identity urn:stdo:concept:traversal-occurrence-profile, calculus_basis_identity, embedded occurrence_signature, occurrence_signature_sha256 and publication_basis containing exactly release_uri, manifest_sha256, member_uri and member_sha256. Its identity is urn:stdo:traversal-occurrence-profile-basis:sha256: followed by sha256 of its RFC 8785 JCS value.

grounding.quote: Tier 3. An optional profile for realising UX surfaces:
This member is material family F20, UX.

concepts.label: UX profile
concepts.definition: Optional Tier 3 UX profile, material family F20, refining DESIGN_MODULE for UX modules. Its own terms include UX surface, State, Msg, Update, View, ViewTree, Cmd, Sub, view-local ephemera, effect membrane, product-truth-changing message, admitted product carrier, Msg-replay test/proof, scaffold, exemption record, UX sprint and its refined result values. It imports FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, SPEC_METHOD and TICKETS under PROFILES without redefining their objects. Graph function and ABG remain graph-execution terms; AssetSurface and workorder remain Product-design carriers.

grounding.quote:
UX surfaces are projection and control surfaces: they render admitted
truth and emit typed messages (P6, P0).

concepts.label: UX surface
concepts.definition: UX surfaces project and control admitted Product truth by rendering it and emitting typed messages. They supplement module realization discipline with render purity, state-transition algebra, effect-membrane discipline and accessibility minimums. In graph-execution Products they are projection and query surfaces.

grounding.quote:
- Update: the pure reducer of signature `(Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`; it
  describes side effects as Cmd values and does not perform them;

concepts.label: Elm Architecture and typed UX process coordinates
concepts.definition: Elm Architecture is the UX constitutional process model: typed runtime-owned State; typed Msg algebra naming every user/system action; pure Update:(Msg,State)→(State,Cmd); pure View:State→ViewTree, producing the same output for the same State; typed Cmd descriptions of scheduled effects and Sub descriptions of external subscriptions interpreted at the runtime's effect membrane. Runtime loop: current State→render View→user Msg→Update produces State and Cmds→runtime interprets Cmds→repeat.

grounding.quote: Such a message maps to one admitted product carrier (P6, P4a):

concepts.label: Admitted UX Product carrier
concepts.definition: Admitted Product carrier for a truth-changing UX message: an AssetSurface action; published graph function or lawful composition; Product-design-admitted workorder, job or runtime command; ABG event/command boundary where ABG is runtime authority; or another typed Product contract named by the design module. AssetSurface or its named equivalent supplies shared typed projections and action contracts.

grounding.quote: The membrane has one job: interpret declared Cmd values.

concepts.label: UX effect membrane
concepts.definition: Declared effect boundary interpreting reducer-produced Cmd values and returning outcomes as typed Msg values. It is the permitted location for I/O, external subscriptions and imperative host-platform interop, rather than a controller or owner of business decisions.

grounding.quote:
The discipline test is the Msg-replay test: can the view's
behaviour be replayed by replaying its Msg log against an empty State?

concepts.label: Msg-replay test and proof
concepts.definition: Msg-replay test asks whether the view's behavior can be reproduced by replaying its Msg log against empty State. Executable Msg-replay proof is recorded work-state resumption evidence that the view owns no hidden continuation. It includes initial State fixture, ordered Msg log, expected final State, expected ordered Cmds, typed Cmd outcome Msgs including every materially possible unresolved outcome and recovery messages, and injected deterministic time, randomness, generated ids and external payloads.

grounding.quote:
The project uses a typed-schema mechanism so that the same type
definition is the source of both compile-time types and runtime
validators; the mechanism choice is project-local.

concepts.label: Shared UX type contract
concepts.definition: Shared front-end/back-end typed contract is the source of UX-consumed types and Product record shapes. A project-local typed-schema mechanism produces both compile-time types and runtime validators from the same definition.

grounding.quote: TICKETS governs ticket and sprint lifecycle;

concepts.label: UX upstream document roles
concepts.definition: Referenced upstream roles: SPEC_METHOD owns constitutional process, authority flow, lawful re-entry, repricing and migration; ODD/graph-execution owns graph-native constructive carrier law; DESIGN_MODULE owns deterministic module realization discipline, including immutability, totality, effect edges, no semantic centre and coupling; TICKETS owns ticket/sprint lifecycle and generic escrow; WORLD_MODEL owns world-model semantic law for Products with that dimension. These are referenced document roles, not imported full definitions.

grounding.quote:
Product authority adopts this profile for a project (§1 Authority), and
the adoption is recorded by (P6, P4b):

concepts.label: UX profile
concepts.definition: The UX profile governs UX surfaces within its adopted or default scope. Product authority adopts it per project, with adoption and any restricted surface scope recorded in design modules.

grounding.quote:
A UX surface that is the public face of a product capability declares
(P2, P6):

concepts.label: UX surface
concepts.definition: A UX interaction surface, including public product capabilities and potentially internal debug, scaffold, prototype or temporary proof surfaces; applicability and exemptions depend on declared scope and the profile's default triggers.

grounding.quote:
4. declaring the State, Msg, Update, Cmd and Sub shapes for each UX
   surface in the design module before implementation;

concepts.label: UX design module
concepts.definition: The design document carrying UX adoption, architecture, surface shapes, contracts, proof references, accessibility refinements and exemptions. Answerability from this document is a basis condition for surface review.

grounding.quote:
A UX sprint may defer local UX
compliance proof during a short iteration window when per-change proof
cost is higher than expected correction cost. This is a cost-optimisation
rule; it does not weaken the UX process model (P2).

concepts.label: UX sprint compliance escrow
concepts.definition: A short UX iteration window permitting specified local compliance proof to be deferred when per-change proof cost exceeds expected correction cost, followed by forensic close review.

grounding.quote:
Purpose and material relation: this profile's verdicts decide closure of a UX surface
and enter conjunctions with the results of other members, which combine
only in the core, so a review, a proof, a closure claim and a carrier
check are each read for their own predicate and none is read as another
(P5, P6).

concepts.label: UX result refinements
concepts.definition: Four predicate-specific result refinements: surface review, replay proof, closure obligations and carrier admission. Their values map individually to core results and combine with other members' results only in the core.

grounding.quote:
Direction: profile to tier 2; preserved meaning: the tier-2 escrow law
applies unchanged to the bound objects;

relations.meaning: UX binds TICKETS replay-proof escrow to §8 Msg-replay proof and changed public-function/carrier contracts to §7 AssetSurface/equivalent typed contract. Tier-2 escrow meaning is preserved, scope narrowed to governed UX surfaces; changed proof or bound-contract definitions require binding re-evaluation.
conditions: For UX surfaces governed by this profile.

grounding.quote:
This profile refines DESIGN_MODULE with the
additional rules a module needs when it realises a UX surface

relations.meaning: UX adds surface realization discipline to referenced DESIGN_MODULE discipline while preserving the parent's governed concerns.
conditions: A module realizes a UX surface.

grounding.quote: Such a message maps to one admitted product carrier (P6, P4a):

relations.meaning: Truth-changing UX action depends on one admitted Product carrier; absence blocks until carrier authoring or repricing.
conditions: The surface's Msg changes Product truth.
exceptions: Genuinely view-local Msg does not trigger this carrier requirement.

grounding.quote:
The membrane interprets Cmd values
produced by the reducer and translates side-effect outcomes back into Msg
values delivered to the reducer.

relations.meaning: Effect membrane consumes the process model's declared Cmd values and returns typed outcome Msg to its reducer; it acquires no controller authority.

grounding.quote:
A UX surface is governed by this profile by default when any of these are
true (P6, P5):

relations.meaning: The source explicitly makes profile law applicable to triggered surfaces, subject to recorded scope.
conditions: At least one default-governance trigger holds.
exceptions: A qualifying recorded scaffold/debug/prototype/temporary-proof exemption governs its scope.

grounding.quote: Only Product authority adopts the profile

constraints.statement: The profile grants no semantic, operation, evaluation, admission, decision, correction, continuation or closure authority. Every material operation/judgment resolves an existing owner-issued grant; copying records or adopting the profile transfers none. Only Product authority adopts it. Adoption declares at least exact profile basis, subject and subject-binding interpretation, Product-concept mappings to sorts/relations, operation/actor/executor/admission/projection/decision authorities, event scope/frontier laws, invalidation/re-entry conditions and qualification evidence of no lost Product distinction. Absent/incomplete adoption means available but inactive for that Product.

grounding.quote:
The list is free of duplicates and sorted by ascending unsigned
UTF-16 code units.

constraints.statement: occurrence_signature_clause_refs is a nonempty duplicate-free list sorted by ascending unsigned UTF-16 code units, containing exactly absolute publication member URIs with fragments #authority-and-adoption, #candidate-judgment-event-and-relation-separation, #causality-and-typed-lineage, #closed-constraint-judgment-residual-and-stop-kinds, #closed-event-kind-population, #closed-relation-families, #closed-semantic-object-sorts, #event-frontier-and-projection, #mutable-subject-effect-relation and #occurrence-identity. These collectively define closed sorts, fields, domains, relations, constraints, judgments, residuals, stops and functor refs. profile_member_sha256 equals publication member digest. The calculus clause resolves exact inherited signature schema/record law in its exact publication. Relative paths, mutable source URIs, missing fragments, duplicates or references outside the two exact publication members refuse the signature.
conditions: Once immutable publication member bytes exist.

grounding.quote:
Its spelling establishes
identity, not acceptance or release standing.

constraints.statement: Embedded signature digest equals its RFC 8785 JCS digest. Basis likewise uses JCS, rejecting duplicate object names before canonicalization. Imported AxiomaticCalculusBasis resolves exact RFC 8785 bytes satisfying referenced calculus §8; its calculated identity equals both calculus_basis_identity fields. Manifest digest resolves exact manifest bytes containing calculus member path/digest once; member bytes match; calculus clause URI is that member plus #2-signature. Derivation/publication bases bind the same immutable package but preserve distinct premise/owner versus publication roles. Principle refs are exactly the sorted duplicate-free expansion declared by that calculus member, never a subset or invented list. Every referenced member's digest occurs once in the manifest and each fragment resolves one heading under publication address law. Unresolved basis, mismatched manifest/member, missing/extra principle refs, invented/absent fragments or unbound bytes refuse admission. Profile member obeys the same rules; mutable paths, strategy posts, implementations and consumer mappings substitute for neither basis nor publication identity. release_uri is one absolute immutable stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<positive-ordinal>/ URI; acceptance is a verdict on that cut, creates no second identity, and is not established by spelling. member_uri is release_uri plus standards/TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md; manifest contains that path/digest exactly once and signature repeats the digest. Kind/version values are exact; digests use lowercase sha256:<64-hex>. Identity preimages are exact JCS values: alternate bytes, newline, object order, duplicate names, non-I-JSON values or implementation-specific serialization cannot acquire the declared identity.
constraints.uncertainty: No instantiated publication basis, manifest or byte-resolution evidence is supplied.

grounding.quote:
Any change to the calculus basis, the signature refs, the closed signature
or the profile member bytes mints a new profile basis.

constraints.statement: Changes to calculus basis, signature refs, closed signature or profile bytes mint a new profile basis. Supersession is an external Product/release judgment; old bases never silently advance. Instances of signature and basis are issued only after member bytes freeze and excluded from the member set whose manifest digest they name. Their member schemas embed neither instance nor instance digest, preventing self-dependent digest preimages.

grounding.quote: - a process, traversal, retry, continuation or closure engine;

constraints.statement: Profile is neither a change to pure a_c/reference-frame law nor mandatory for all symbolic models; neither concrete subject/workspace ontology nor process/traversal/retry/continuation/closure engine; neither event store/log schema/projection implementation/state carrier nor mutation/admission/evaluation/decision authority; neither prospective-frame nor sensor-population profile. It guarantees neither occurrence ownership of every event nor acyclicity of every typed-lineage graph.

grounding.quote: Review and qualification cover at least (P6, P5):

constraints.statement: Review covers at least: exact a_c basis/eight RecordKind_ac populations/closed domains without shadowing; inherited families/direct coordinates/disjoint local-external identities; complete seeds/congruent mirrors/no future results/events; first event without fictional predecessor; distinct candidate/judgment/event/relation/cut/cut-judgment ids with unchanged subject digest; idempotent or refused duplicates; cycles in each identity/causal subgraph; lawful opposing support/correction; closed event kinds/payload/digest/scope/bindings without fabricated event_for; separated functor/traversal/operation-kind/instance/executor/actor/grant/invocation/target/territory; missing/stale/mismatched/out-of-territory grants; all four effect cases; mutable reality carrier; fresh reapplication identities; component/aggregate identities; refusal on stale pre-observation and grant currentness; incomplete cut refusal including missing/non-admitted cut judgment or unequal source frontiers; frontier completeness/staleness/correction selection; no cause from timestamp/ordinal/adjacency/containment/correlation; absent adoption and incomplete-mapping refusal; exact JCS/kind/schema/URI/digest/calculus-address/publication-membership reconstruction. Examples/checkers establish only evaluated claims and acquire no engine or semantic authority.
constraints.uncertainty: The conformance list uses 'refusal' for stale readiness while the detailed law distinguishes stale, hold and stale_currentness.
conditions: For review and qualification of an adoption/implementation.

grounding.quote: The view is not a state owner.

constraints.statement: View is a pure projection of typed State; transitions are pure reductions over typed Msg; effects are reducer-described values interpreted at a declared membrane; runtime owns lifecycle and continuation. Stateful mutation in views, two-way binding without action emission and effect handlers acting as controllers violate the profile despite ecosystem convention.
conditions: For UX work governed by this profile.
exceptions: The narrowly conditioned view-local ephemera allowance is stated separately.

grounding.quote:
until one of them is taken, the ambiguity is
`blocked` and implementation does not proceed.

constraints.statement: Adopted profile is the surface's sole UX realization authority. Project ADRs may choose stack but cannot weaken process model. Existing code, library convention, screenshots, comments, design history, prototypes and generated artifacts are evidence only. Concrete ambiguity fails closed: satisfy stricter interpretation→resolved; reprice through governing constitutional method to governing-surface owner→escalated; record scoped design-module exemption before implementation→carried with exemption residual. Until an exit is taken, ambiguity is blocked and implementation cannot proceed.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced §15 gives further result definitions outside the supplied sections.
conditions: Product authority adopts the profile for a UX surface and records adoption in product definition, ticket, design module or review.

grounding.quote:
Its instance
premises hold where a UX surface is realised under this profile; they are
adopted with it and do not follow from the foundations

constraints.statement: F20 imports F2 transitions/steps/configuration, F3 results/combination, F4 work-state/resumption/reuse, F11 change/ambiguity and F13 carriers, and refines F17 software design. Adopted instance premises, not foundational deductions, are: I1 people/systems observe admitted truth and request changes through surfaces; I2 external Product design declares truth/carriers; I3 stacks differ and tolerate view state/continuation/effects; I4 uncontrolled data seams; I5 short iterations can make per-change proof cost exceed correction. Ten authored consequence rows preserve ownership: (1) P6/P1+F2/F11+I1/I2 require admitted carriers and blocking absent carriers; profile owns five carrier kinds/binding requirements, Product design actual contracts. (2) P0/P1/P4a+F2+I3 support typed transitions; choosing TEA and ephemera test is profile policy. (3) P0/P5+F2 require declared effects; profile owns membrane/handler rules refining DESIGN_MODULE, project interpreter. (4) P4b/P6+F4 require replayable recorded behavior and executable proof before closure; profile owns test/six proof contents, project design module proof surface. (5) P3/P1/P6+I4 require shared types and runtime validation; profile makes six seams mandatory, project schema mechanism. (6) P2/P6+I1 require public-capability accessibility declarations and recorded internal-debug exemption; profile owns five declarations, WCAG AA is only recommended web default, project may strengthen. (7) P2/P1+I3 permit stack freedom, never rankings; project owns choices, profile owns compliance tests and stricter fail-closed handling. (8) P6+F11+I3 require admitted adoption/one authority and ambiguity outcomes. (9) P6/P4b+F4/F11/F13+I5 require authorized scoped scaffold exemption with retirement, no production by accumulation, visible bounded payable proof escrow and classification of every close finding; profile owns default-governance/escrow/trigger choices, TICKETS generic escrow and six close classifications, SPEC_METHOD sprint boundary. (10) P5/P6+F3 require four predicate-specific refinements, one core mapping per value without conflating review/replay/closure/carrier results. Pillar associations by row are respectively {4,5,9},{3,4},{4,8},{6,8,9},{2,3,4},{1,9},{4,8},{1,7,9},{1,9},{3,9}. P0 is recovered; P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 independent; P5 derives from P0/P6 with open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts. No policy choice is presented as foundational derivation. Adoption-opening steps, failure patterns and review questions apply these consequences; each clause names its requiring principle.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed five accessibility declarations, default-governance conditions, escrow inventories, classifications and four result refinements are referenced but not enumerated in the supplied source.
conditions: Instance premises hold where a UX surface is realized under this adopted profile.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Authored consumer loci remain directional applications, not extra authority: carrier row→ACTIVATION §2, relationship clause, both realization tests, adoption step5, escrow, failures7/13, review3/4, §15 carrier/block results; process row→both tests, adoption4/9, failures1/2/8/10, review1/2/6/10/11, surface review; membrane row→discretion, transitions, view shape, adoption6/9, failures3/5/11, review5/10, surface review; replay row→adoption7, escrow, failures4/12, review7/12, replay/closure results; types row→discretion, failures6/14, review8/9, surface review; accessibility row→adoption8, escrow, failure9, review10, closure; stack row→adoption2, review11, stricter §15 review; authority row→adoption, failure16, §15 fail-closed; scaffold/escrow row→relationship, failures15/17, review10/14, closure and §15 scope/classification boundary; results row→authority, carriers and both tests. Consumers decide nothing beyond owning sections. No other member returns the UX refined values, and FOUNDATIONS owns their core without applying this UX section's rule.
constraints.uncertainty: Most target loci are not supplied; their detailed rules cannot be reconstructed from consumer indexes.
conditions: When consumers enter the foundation-to-law rows.

grounding.quote:
- when a module realises a non-UX surface, only DESIGN_MODULE applies, and
  its design module ignores this profile;

constraints.statement: UX refines rather than duplicates DESIGN_MODULE: parent-governed immutability, totality, effect edges, no semantic centre and coupling remain parent law; UX extends render lifecycle, browser events, layout and accessibility. For a UX module, both apply and its design module reads both; for a non-UX module, only DESIGN_MODULE applies and UX is ignored. A graph-execution Product projection/query surface including UX follows UX realization law. Graph execution determines Product graph-native shape, DESIGN_MODULE module discipline, UX additional surface discipline.

grounding.quote:
UX work may use sprint
compliance escrow under §12 when the sprint boundary makes deferred proof
visible, bounded and payable.

constraints.statement: UX sprint compliance escrow is permitted under referenced §12 only when the sprint boundary makes deferred proof visible, bounded and payable. WORLD_MODEL governs world-model semantic law only for Products with that dimension; UX over world-model state still binds AssetSurface or equivalent under §7.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed escrow and world-model laws are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Those are valid concerns; they
belong in product-local surfaces, not in this constitutional profile (P2).

constraints.statement: UX profile does not supply styling/design-system specification, component library, brand/visual identity, wireframing/prototyping process, user-study method, stack ranking or framework recommendation. These valid concerns belong to Product-local surfaces.

grounding.quote:
If no
admitted carrier exists for a product-truth-changing message, the UX
surface is blocked until the carrier is authored or the requirement is
repriced

constraints.statement: Every Product-truth-changing message maps to one admitted Product carrier. Such changes include asset writes/creation/moves/deletion; Context, selection authority, pinning/global state; session spawning/attachment/resumption; agent/job/workorder/graph-call/runtime-command dispatch; closure/approval/continuation/lineage/provenance/evidence; publishing/accepting/rejecting/superseding records. UX cannot become a hidden constructive carrier. Without an admitted carrier, surface is blocked until one is authored or requirement repriced.
conditions: A Msg changes Product truth.
exceptions: UX-local messages may govern genuinely view-local expansion, sort, filter, focus and draft concerns.

grounding.quote:
Any
realisation that preserves §4 to §8 is compliant with this profile.

A realisation is compliant with this profile when §4 to §10
hold under inspection and the §13 failure patterns are absent

constraints.statement: Project records chosen stack and short justification in design module. Each discretionary choice must preserve §4 Elm model and §6 membrane. Process model is non-negotiable, stack free within it; profile tests realizations and never ranks frameworks. One clause tests §4–§8; Realisation discretion tests §4–§10 under inspection plus absence of §13 failures. Source explicitly retains this difference for governing authority and refers to §15's stricter fail-closed selection. Reject view-owned state continuation, render effects, state mutation outside typed reducer, multi-step view state machines bypassing Msg, two-way binding without Msg, imperative DOM manipulation in render and handlers used as controllers. Non-normative examples are language-integrated reducers, typed reducer plus effect interpreter, reactive signals behind reducer with no external signal mutation, and server-rendered hypermedia using server derivation and request/response effect boundary; examples confer no compliance verdict.
constraints.uncertainty: Full §13 and §15 are absent; no implementation's compliance is evaluated.
conditions: For a project selecting a realization stack.

grounding.quote:
A lost or failed transport reply alone
establishes neither completion nor non-completion.

constraints.statement: Surface declares State shape, Msg algebra, pure Update:(Msg,State)→(State,Cmd), Cmd algebra and conditional Sub algebra. State changes through typed Msg reduction. Each Cmd names effect kind, typed input, admitted carrier/external target, typed outcome Msg family covering every materially possible observed or unresolved result including success/failure, outcome-selection evidence and observations resolving uncertainty, and any required deterministic correlation among Cmd, invocation, outcome messages and replay. Outcome Msg represents available evidence; intended-effect meanings completed, not_effected, completion_unknown answer 'the intended effect occurred' without replacing Product message vocabulary. Lost/failed transport alone proves neither completion nor non-completion; sufficient independent observation may decide, otherwise Msg and State retain completion_unknown, correlation and missing observation. Reducer performs no I/O, side-channel logging or global mutation; runtime interprets effects at membrane.
exceptions: Sub algebra is required when subscribing to external or runtime events.

grounding.quote:
Recovery is an
explicit Cmd/Msg interaction, not hidden membrane continuation

constraints.statement: Effects are isolated to declared membrane. It interprets reducer-produced Cmd and returns outcomes through Msg; branching, conditional state derivation and multi-step business decisions belong in reducer. One declared Cmd is interpreted per effect. Unresolved outcome returns typed unresolved Msg without coercion to success/failure. Before repetition or dependent effect whose safety depends on outcome, Product observes owning state and follows referenced recovery with current authority/territory retained; recovery is explicit Cmd/Msg. Any useEffect/createEffect/onMount/subscribe/server-action or other handler belongs to membrane only when interpreting a declared Cmd. A handler deciding transitions violates the law; move that logic to reducer. Render, render helpers and reducer have no I/O, subscription or imperative platform manipulation.
constraints.uncertainty: Full ACTIVATION recovery law is referenced but absent.

grounding.quote:
Absence of an admitted
contract blocks product-truth-changing UX actions

constraints.statement: Bind one or more AssetSurface contracts as data sources/action targets. State derives from their projections without local asset-shape redeclaration. Truth-changing Msg variants map one-to-one to action-registry entries or documented projection wrappers with no hidden semantic change. UX-local variants remain local concerns. Selection emits Context update/equivalent consistent with selection contract. Writes use action registry, never direct file/service calls. Shared typed contract is ground truth on both sides; no admitted equivalent contract means truth-changing actions are blocked.
conditions: When Product publishes typed AssetSurface contracts under graph-execution carrier law and Product design.
exceptions: Without AssetSurface, the design module names an equivalent typed contract and applies the same law.

grounding.quote:
If the prompt cannot identify that
carrier and action path, the correct result is a block or re-entry, not
local UI invention

constraints.statement: A UI/operator work prompt carries needed governing UX law using a current derived surface/projected frame where suitable, otherwise deciding sections directly, rather than requiring raw-member rediscovery. If work changes Product truth through UI, prompt names admitted carrier and action path; failure to identify them yields block/re-entry rather than local invention. This is a represented prompt-processing requirement, not an instruction to execute that workflow here.
constraints.uncertainty: Acquisition mechanics are owned by absent ACTIVATION §2.
conditions: For source-described prompt construction for UI/operator-surface work.

grounding.quote:
A view does not:

- decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event;

constraints.statement: Runtime owns continuation; view owns none. All transitions use declared Msg interpreted by reducer. View cannot independently decide next state, chain local updates without separate Msg emissions or hide inter-event state in refs, closures or module variables. A needed multi-step machine belongs in reducer State with explicit phase Msg; view projects the phase. Inability to replay behavior from Msg log against empty State indicates leaked view continuation.

grounding.quote:
`replay_passes` can coexist with `completion_unknown` for the
effect predicate

constraints.statement: Require at least one executable replay proof per Product-meaningful interaction family, with all six declared proof components. Correctness depending on unrepresented DOM state; mutable refs/module variables/closures/timers/handler memory; network/file results bypassing Msg; or local state affecting Product after unmount/replay fails proof. Where effect may be unresolved, cover correlated unresolved Msg, retained State and recovery, including no outcome-dependent repeat before required observation. Reproducing that State proves only replay, never external completion: replay_passes and completion_unknown may coexist. Projection-only no-effect proof can be Msg log, final State and empty Cmd sequence.
conditions: Before a Product UX surface claims closure under the profile.
exceptions: A pure projection-only surface may use a no-effect proof.

constraints.statement: View accepts typed State/props/context, returns typed ViewTree, declares every consumed input, captures no mutable cross-render closure state and reads no undeclared source. Function/component/template/server handler/signal expression/other framework shape is a recorded stack decision; constitutional State→ViewTree and no body side effects remain. An effect-handler-written ref read during rendering violates §6 unless covered by the narrow declared-membrane exception.
constraints.uncertainty: The membrane-handle exception does not expressly waive typed inputs, declared reads or replay requirements.
exceptions: Out-of-render mutation is excepted from the cited §6 violation when part of declared membrane, such as a design-module-named imperative-interop platform handle.

grounding.quote: Runtime validation is mandatory at every untrusted or out-of-process seam

constraints.statement: Import UX-consumed/back-end shapes from shared front/back contract rather than redeclaring them; same package or contracts/ package is typical, not mandatory. Runtime validation is obligatory for HTTP/RPC responses, MCP payloads, file-loaded records, websocket/event streams, agent/worker outputs and URL/storage/clipboard/browser integration payloads. One typed-schema definition produces compile-time types and runtime validators; mechanism is project-local. Compile-time TypeScript alone is insufficient. View-local form drafts, sort enums and filter strings may have local types without shadowing back-end types.
conditions: At every untrusted or out-of-process seam.
exceptions: UX-local types may describe view-local concerns but cannot shadow back-end types.

grounding.quote:
- semantic structure (heading levels, landmarks, lists, or
  platform-equivalent affordances);
- keyboard or platform-equivalent navigability for every action that has
  a pointer interaction;
- focus management on dynamic content changes;
- accessibility annotations for any custom interactive element that lacks
  a native semantic equivalent;
- colour contrast at the project's declared accessibility standard (WCAG

Accessibility is not optional for product capabilities. It is optional
for internal-only debug surfaces, and the design module records the
exemption (P2, P6). This section is intentionally minimal. Projects with
stricter accessibility obligations (regulated industry, public-sector
procurement) author a project-local accessibility refinement and cite it
from their design modules (P2).

constraints.statement: Declare semantic structure or platform equivalents; keyboard or platform-equivalent navigation for every pointer action; focus management for dynamic changes; annotations for every custom interactive element lacking native semantics; and contrast at the project's declared standard. WCAG AA is a recommended web default, not an unconditional mandate. Projects with stricter obligations author a local accessibility refinement and cite it from design modules.
constraints.uncertainty: Other supplied sections mention recorded public-surface exemptions; their relationship to this section's non-optional language is retained as a residual.
conditions: The UX surface is the public face of a product capability.
exceptions: Accessibility is optional for internal-only debug surfaces, with the exemption recorded in the design module.

conditions: Any one trigger holds: reachable from product shell; used as proof for a ticket, requirement, design module, release or review; can mutate product truth; can spawn, attach, resume or dispatch work; or can change Context, selection authority, closure, continuation, evidence or provenance.
exceptions: A scaffold, prototype, debug pane or temporary proof surface can be exempt only with the specified record.

If one of those appears, the sprint records the finding and the work

grounding.quote:
A UX sprint should close when continued iteration is more expensive or
less trustworthy than review. Valid close triggers include (P2, P6):

UX sprint close is a forensic walkthrough: it reviews each changed
screen, state and product-meaningful interaction against the cited
authority (P6). Each finding takes one of the six classifications of
TICKETS §3 Close review (`accepted`, `local_paydown`, `design_reframe`,
`requirement_reprice`, `product_reprice`, `remove`); for a UX finding,
`accepted` reads as compliant with this profile and the cited design,
and `local_paydown` as local UX debt captured by a paydown ticket (P6,
P5). The sprint may close with explicit local paydown tickets only where
the debt is local to UX realisation and the governing method allows
follow-up. It may not close while product-truth carrier gaps, hidden
state continuation or authority drift remain unclassified (P6, P4b).

Closure under this profile for a product UX surface still requires the
§8 Msg-replay proof and the §11 accessibility obligations unless an
explicit exemption is recorded. The sprint can defer those obligations
during iteration; it cannot erase them (P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: A sprint should close when further iteration is costlier or less trustworthy than review. Valid triggers include timebox expiry, too many changed states for casual review, obsolete screenshots/walkthroughs, interaction changes beyond polish, or reviewer uncertainty requiring reconciliation. Close reviews every changed screen, state and meaningful interaction against cited authority, classifying every finding as accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice or remove. Accepted means profile-and-design compliant; local_paydown means local UX debt captured by ticket. Unclassified carrier gaps, hidden state continuation or authority drift prohibit close. Replay and accessibility obligations may be deferred, never erased.
constraints.uncertainty: The six classifications are TICKETS-owned and are not mapped by the UX result section.
conditions: UX sprint close is considered or claimed.
exceptions: Explicitly recorded exemptions can cover replay or accessibility closure obligations.
Explicit local paydown tickets permit close only for debt local to UX realisation and only where the governing method allows follow-up.

grounding.quote: A UX surface violates this profile when any of these are true (P6, P5):

Any of these is a violation of this profile. Repeated violations are not
normalised by usage; they are repaired or the surface is repriced (P6,
P4b).

constraints.statement: Each independently constitutes a violation: render code directly mutates state/props/context; view-local cells carry product meaning rather than ephemera; effect-handler conditional logic decides transitions; multistep state machines live in views instead of reducers; render reads mutable refs outside the declared membrane; UX-local types shadow/redeclare backend types instead of importing shared contracts; selection/action emission writes file/network without AssetSurface action; unrecorded view-shape exemption; public-capability accessibility omitted without recorded exemption; two-way binding emits no typed Msg and bypasses reducer; Cmd logic implemented imperatively inside an effect handler; behaviour unreplayable from Msg log against empty State; truth-changing message lacks admitted carrier, graph function, runtime command or typed product contract; external data enters UX state without runtime validation; reachable, mutating or proof-used scaffold/debug surface lacks §12 exemption record; local ADR/convention/existing code weakens the profile; sprint claims closure with deferred proof, accessibility, carrier, scaffold or authority debt unclassified or un-ticketed. Repetition does not normalise violations: repair or reprice.
conditions: Any listed failure pattern is present on a surface to which the profile applies.
exceptions: The source expressly conditions view-shape and accessibility failures on absence of recorded exemptions; scaffold failure refers to its required exemption record.

grounding.quote: A UX surface review under this profile should answer (P6, P2):

If any of these cannot be answered, the design module is incomplete (P6,
P5).

constraints.statement: Review should answer: State/Msg/Update; Cmd/Sub algebra; bound contracts; truth-changing messages' admitted carriers; membrane location and interpreted Cmds; provable View=f(State) purity; Msg-log replay proof; shared-contract import of all consumed types; runtime validation of all out-of-process payloads; documented view/membrane/accessibility/scaffold/debug exemptions; chosen stack's preservation of the Elm process model; non-ownership of replay continuation by the view; design-module carrier set and structural diagram for closure; and, if a sprint was used, classification of every deferred proof/accessibility/carrier/scaffold/authority finding. Any unanswerable question makes the design module incomplete.
constraints.uncertainty: Answerability is not an instruction to evaluate a particular surface here.
conditions: A UX surface review is performed under the profile.
The sprint-specific question applies if the work used a UX sprint.

grounding.quote: | surface review | `design_module_incomplete` | invalid_basis | no counterexample of `violation` is found, and a §14 review question cannot be answered from the design module, so the design module, on which the review rests, cannot support the evaluation; the value names the unanswered question |

Fail closed (§1 Authority). Where this profile is ambiguous for a case,
the surface review applies the stricter interpretation and returns its
value under it; the ambiguity alone never yields `compliant`. Where the
ambiguity leaves a term the review depends on undefined, so that no
stricter interpretation is fixed, the review returns
`out_of_frame` and names the term and its owner
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Out of frame or
indeterminate, first case). A reprice or a scoped exemption, the other
two exits of §1 Authority, is a re-entry or a scope recorded in the
design module, not a value of this section (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: compliant→satisfied requires §§4–10 under inspection, no §13 failure and every §14 question answered from the design module. violation→falsified when a failure pattern, §4-rejected realisation or broken §§4–10 rule supplies a counterexample. design_module_incomplete→invalid_basis applies only with no violation counterexample and an unanswered design-module question, which is named. The source chooses the stricter §§4–10 test over the competing §§4–8 compliance test and retains the disagreement for authority. Ambiguity requires the stricter fixed interpretation; ambiguity alone cannot yield compliant. If an undefined required term prevents fixing a stricter interpretation, return out_of_frame naming term and owner. Repricing and scoped exemption are re-entry/scope, not results.
constraints.uncertainty: The two §4 tests and §1 authority are only described here, not supplied directly.
conditions: A surface review is evaluated on its exact basis.

grounding.quote:
| replay proof | `replay_passes` | satisfied | the proof reproduces its expected final State and ordered Cmd values on its injected deterministic values, and no dependency that §8 lists decides its correctness; reproducing an unresolved outcome proves replay only and does not establish external completion |
| replay proof | `replay_fails` | falsified | the proof diverges from its expected final State or Cmd values, or its correctness depends on something §8 lists; the divergence or the dependency is the counterexample |
| closure obligations | `closure_obligations_met` | satisfied | every product-meaningful interaction family carries its Msg-replay proof and the surface its accessibility declarations, or a recorded exemption covers the obligation |
| closure obligations | `closure_unproven` | falsified | an interaction family lacks its proof or the surface an accessibility declaration, with no recorded exemption; that family or obligation is the counterexample. Inside an open UX sprint closure is not claimed, and a deferred obligation is escrow under §12 |
| carrier admission | `carrier_admitted` | satisfied | each product-truth-changing message or action maps to an admitted carrier of §3 and binds under §7 to an AssetSurface contract where the product publishes one, otherwise to the equivalent typed contract its design module names |
| carrier admission | `carrier_missing` | falsified | a product-truth-changing message or action has no admitted carrier or typed contract (§13 pattern 13); that message or action is the counterexample |

constraints.statement: For replay: replay_passes→satisfied iff injected deterministic values reproduce expected final State and ordered Cmds without a §8-prohibited correctness dependency; replay_fails→falsified for divergence or such a dependency, naming it. Replaying unresolved outcomes establishes replay only, not external completion. For closure: closure_obligations_met→satisfied requires every meaningful interaction family's proof and surface accessibility declarations or applicable recorded exemptions; closure_unproven→falsified identifies a missing uncovered proof/declaration. For carrier admission: carrier_admitted→satisfied requires every truth-changing message/action to map to a §3-admitted carrier and bind to the published AssetSurface contract, otherwise the equivalent typed contract named in the design module; carrier_missing→falsified identifies a message/action without admitted carrier or typed contract.
constraints.uncertainty: The §8 forbidden-dependency list and detailed carrier admission law are outside the supplied source.
conditions: The relevant predicate is evaluated; closure obligations apply where product-UX closure is claimed.
exceptions: A recorded exemption can cover a closure obligation.
Inside an open UX sprint closure is not claimed; deferred obligations are escrow.

grounding.quote:
Where none of these values applies, the evaluation returns a core value
directly under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results):
`indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot decide its predicate,
naming the evidence that would decide; `out_of_frame` where its claim
needs a relation or capability that its frame does not declare; and
`invalid_basis` where its subject or basis cannot support it on a ground
other than `design_module_incomplete` (P5).

Two collisions are resolved here (P1): "blocked" for want of a carrier is
not the ambiguity outcome `blocked` of
[ACTIVATION §3 Ambiguity outcome](ACTIVATION.md#ambiguity-outcome), and
`design_module_incomplete` is not the value `incomplete` of ACTIVATION §3
Construction availability. An exempt scaffold is a recorded scope (§12),
not a result; evaluations outside its recorded scope proceed under this
section. The six close classifications of §12 belong to TICKETS §3 and are
not mapped here (P6).

constraints.statement: Every mapping carries its own predicate, maps to exactly one core result and cannot raise standing or satisfy another predicate. Where no refinement applies, return indeterminate for undecidable admissible evidence and name deciding evidence; out_of_frame for undeclared required relation/capability; invalid_basis for unsupported subject/basis other than design_module_incomplete. Missing carrier yields carrier_missing for admission and violation for review; a construction step needing it stops with re_entry_requested(authority), naming carrier, design owner and re-entry to author it or reprice the requirement. This is distinct from ACTIVATION ambiguity blocked; design_module_incomplete is distinct from construction incomplete. Exempt scaffold is scope, not result; evaluations outside its scope use this algebra. TICKETS close classes are not mapped here.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION owns the construction-stop mapping; its full semantics are not supplied.
